applied.name: hexanedinitrile
applied.value: Primary ThermoML observation confirmed at 298.15 K: eps=32.12 +/- 0.1, pure component, zero frequency, dataset 3, DOI 10.1021/je300958c. ECW-308 Table S3 lists this compound with a value of 30.00 at 25 C citing Duncan, Salem & Abu-Lebdeh, J. Electrochem. Soc. 2013, 160, A838 (DOI 10.1149/2.088306jes). That cited table was retrieved on 2026-09-24 from the NRC Publications Archive accepted manuscript (record 431ad01c-3fb7-4610-923b-99d08c6a4c16): Table I on p. A840 reports the compound as eps=30, not 30.00, so the two decimals in ECW-308 are unsupported precision rather than a second measurement. The paper records that dielectric constants were measured with a Brookhaven BI-870 meter, but Table I carries no per-row provenance, temperature, frequency or uncertainty, so the value cannot be promoted to a same-condition primary cross-check. It sits about 6.6% below the retained primary observation and is recorded as a source disagreement rather than an error. The values were not averaged.
applied.rationale: Appendix J requires a conflict record against the retained primary value, and now that the cited original table has been retrieved the record must state what that source actually reports instead of saying it was not retrieved.

applied.name: 3-methoxypropionitrile
applied.previous_value: Value 36.00 at 25 C was read from the ECW-308 battery-solvent compilation (Wang et al. 2023, Adv. Funct. Mater., DOI 10.1002/adfm.202212342, Table S3, rows 43 and 51), which cites Perricone et al. (2013) Electrochim. Acta 93, 1 (DOI 10.1016/j.electacta.2013.01.084). The cited primary paper is closed access and could not be retrieved, and no second independent source was found, so the value is recorded as a secondary compilation and the row is deliberately held out of the model-ready set pending primary confirmation. The publisher supplementary file itself is not redistributable; only the numeric fact is recorded.
applied.value: Value 36.00 at 25 C was read from the ECW-308 battery-solvent compilation (Wang et al. 2023, Adv. Funct. Mater., DOI 10.1002/adfm.202212342, Table S3, rows 43 and 51), which cites Perricone et al. (2013) Electrochim. Acta 93, 1 (DOI 10.1016/j.electacta.2013.01.084). The cited paper is closed access, but the same first author's open-access doctoral thesis (Perricone 2011, Universite de Grenoble, NNT 2011GRENI032, HAL tel-00630049) gives eps_r = 36 with an explicit 25 C condition in two tables a reader can open: Tableau 4 (printed page 28), whose permittivity column is headed 'eps_r a 25 C', and Tableau 14 (printed page 77), whose property row is headed 'Constante dielectrique a 25 C' and which gives 36 in its MP column. The same thesis also lists eps_r = 36 in Tableau 12 (printed page 65), which carries no temperature note; an earlier provenance pass read only that table and therefore recorded the temperature as unstated. The temperature is thus corroborated at document level, but the thesis belongs to the same research line as the cited paper, so this is not a second measurement and the value stays a secondary compilation. The row is a curated exclusion (data/processed/dielectric_v03_exclusions.csv: secondary compilation awaiting primary confirmation), and that exclusion is what sets model_ready=false; the row also has no GFN2-xTB physical-feature row at all - an independent precondition, and not part of the failed_physical_feature_* bucket, which only counts feature rows that exist with status=error. Both blockers would have to clear before the value could be fitted. The temperature question is no longer part of this row's blocker list. The publisher supplementary file and the thesis PDF are not redistributable; only the numeric facts are recorded. Adversarial Table S3 review also found that row 51's dielectric cell contains a stacked 25.00 value without a separate citation; the cited main value 36.00 is retained, and 25.00 is recorded as a multi-value warning rather than averaged or promoted.
applied.rationale: Record the adversarial multi-value warning from the ECW-308 Table S3 review without promoting or averaging the stacked 25.00 value.
